title: Nephrotic vs Nephritic Syndrome
subtitle: Compare presentation, labs, and biopsy clues

steps.title: Nephrotic syndrome
steps.body: Heavy proteinuria (>3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminemia, edema, hyperlipidemia. Urine shows fatty casts and oval fat bodies.
steps.tip: Minimal change disease is most common in children.

steps.title: Nephritic syndrome
steps.body: Hematuria with dysmorphic RBCs and RBC casts, hypertension, oliguria, and subnephrotic proteinuria.
steps.tip: RBC casts = glomerular inflammation until proven otherwise.

steps.title: Complement studies
steps.body: Low C3 suggests MPGN, post-streptococcal GN, or C3 glomerulopathy. Normal complement in IgA nephropathy and ANCA vasculitis.
steps.tip: Low C3 and C4 suggests lupus nephritis.

steps.title: Common nephrotic causes
steps.body: Adults: FSGS, membranous nephropathy, diabetic nephropathy. Children: minimal change disease.
steps.tip: Membranous associated with PLA2R antibodies in many adults.

steps.title: Common nephritic causes
steps.body: IgA nephropathy, post-infectious GN, lupus, ANCA vasculitis, anti-GBM disease.
steps.tip: Rapidly progressive GN needs urgent biopsy and immunosuppression.
